description.narrative:
The partnership between the Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the World Climate Foundation (WCF), with support from Climate Investment Coalition (CIC) is to establish WCF in the role of operating partner for IMCA for a suggested period covering 2023-2026. As IMCA Partner, WCF will support the successful outcomes of IMCA, playing a key role in project planning and coordination, stakeholder outreach and engagement, and communicating its achievements through side events and high-profiled announcements to support IMCA’s role in creating climate investments in emerging markets.
IMCA is a unique partnership between the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida), Denmark’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Finland’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs (as a starting point, with new country partners to be considered once established). Its role will be to create concrete blended finance investment pipeline collaboration, establish blended finance vehicles, and catalyse private sector funding into climate in emerging markets and developing economies (Official development assistance (ODA) countries specifically).

title.narrative: Workstream 1: Cordinated collaboration between IMCA partners on pipeline transactions Workstreamt 2: Effective communication, leading to a series of blended finance funds launched by end of 2025 Workstream 3: Focus on broader SDG focus, call for proposals aiming to launch 1-2 proposals for origination of blended finance funds by end of 2026.

Workstream 1 Workstream 1a: Regular technical level meetings on pipeline information sharing, leading to at least 5 transactions per year entered into and/or collaborated on by IMCA partners. Aggregated amounts of donor concessional capital and mobilised private capital through IMCA cooperation will be reported annually by WCF. Workstream 1b: An accessible and GDPR-compatible mechanism for pipeline information sharing ready and used by IMCA country partners by 2025, with set guidelines no disclosure requirements.
Workstream 2 Workstream 2a: 3-5 call for proposals launched by end of 2025, leading to origination of at least 3-5 blended finance funds and more in 2026. Workstream 2a: Mobilisation of billions of USD in private capital combined for investments in emerging markets and developing economies. Process structured and facilitated through CFDA with support from Operating Partner (WCF). WCF to report on combined donor catalytic capital and private capital mobilised, in terms of total financial closes catalysed and according to the OECD DAC rules on leverage calculations on private capital mobilization. Combined finance pledge on catalytic donor capital in the scale of millions of USD to support COP28 launch of IMCA and call for proposal. WCF to report on combined donor capital pledged (beyond committed) to the end of 2025.
Workstream 3: Reporting of successes and challenges on Workstream 1 and 2, leading to development of broader SDG focused strategy and call for proposals. Determine theme and regional focus to launch 1-2 call for proposals by end of 2026.

target.value:
The establishment and operation of IMCA, leading to collaboration between established and experienced stakeholders, scaled blended finance, concrete pipeline collaboration and creation of new transactions on climate investments in developing countries.
An outcome report is to be consolidated anually across the IMCA workstream 1 and workstream 2 summarizing the IMCA transactions and the impacts expected to be achieved by the transaction including e.g. On GHG emissions avoided, new renewable generation capacity expected to be installed in Mw, decent jobs expected to created etc.
